quilt-forge-main/.github/workflows/forge:
name: forge

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      test-cmd:
        required: true
        type: string
      roots:
        required: false
        type: string
        default: "7,11,23"
      node-version:
        required: false
        type: string
        default: "22"
      python-version:
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ""
      probe-only:
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false

jobs:
  probe:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: checkout forge tools
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          repository: SuperInstance/quilt-forge
          ref: v0
          path: .forge
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: ${{ inputs.node-version }}
      - name: probe repo shape
        run: node .forge/tools/forge-probe.mjs --out forge-probe.json
      - name: upload probe receipt
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: forge-probe
          path: forge-probe.json
      - name: print shape
        run: cat forge-probe.json

  receipts:
    needs: probe
    if: ${{ inputs.probe-only == false }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: checkout forge tools
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          repository: SuperInstance/quilt-forge
          ref: v0
          path: .forge
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: ${{ inputs.node-version }}
      - if: ${{ inputs.python-version != '' }}
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: ${{ inputs.python-version }}
      - name: run declared command
        run: node .forge/tools/forge-run.mjs "${{ inputs.test-cmd }}" --out forge-receipt.json
      - name: upload run receipt
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: forge-receipt
          path: forge-receipt.json

  roots:
    needs: probe
    if: ${{ inputs.probe-only == false && inputs.roots != '' }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        root: [7, 11, 23]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: checkout forge tools
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          repository: SuperInstance/quilt-forge
          ref: v0
          path: .forge
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: ${{ inputs.node-version }}
      - if: ${{ inputs.python-version != '' }}
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: ${{ inputs.python-version }}
      - name: run under root ${{ matrix.root }}
        if: ${{ contains(inputs.roots, format('{0}', matrix.root)) }}
        run: node .forge/tools/forge-run.mjs "${{ inputs.test-cmd }}" --root ${{ matrix.root }} --out root-receipt-${{ matrix.root }}.json
      - name: upload root receipt
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: root-receipt-${{ matrix.root }}
          path: root-receipt-${{ matrix.root }}.json
          if-no-files-found: ignore

  seal:
    needs: [probe, receipts, roots]
    if: always()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: checkout forge tools
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          repository: SuperInstance/quilt-forge
          ref: v0
          path: .forge
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: ${{ inputs.node-version }}
      - name: gather artifacts
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          path: artifacts
          merge-multiple: true
      - name: seal constellation receipt
        run: node .forge/tools/forge-seal.mjs --dir artifacts --out forge-seal.json
      - name: upload seal
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: forge-seal
          path: |
            forge-seal.json
            artifacts/forge-ledger.jsonl
      - name: print seal
        run: cat forge-seal.json
quilt-forge-main/README.md:
# quilt-forge

The soft CI/CD substrate of the SuperInstance constellation.

**One workflow. Receipts first. Never blocks. Adopt in five minutes.**

quilt-atlas counts 4,854 repos and probed CI on the top-motion slice only — of the
24 most-pushed repos, 15 have no workflows at all, and the nine that do speak nine
dialects (`build.yml`, `smoke.yml`, `garden.yml`, `merge-gate.yml`, twelve files in
one repo). The constellation can't abstract higher while its low level is this
sparse and this snowflaked. The forge is the streamlined low level: a single
reusable workflow every repo calls the same way, producing the same receipts —
soft in its dynamics, so the layers above (atlas telemetry, prospector scoring,
ladder claims) can trust what any repo reports about itself.

## Doctrine

1. **Receipts over gates.** The forge reports; it does not block. A failing test
   under forge produces a red-free run with an honest receipt (`exit: 1`). Softness
   is deliberate: hard gates get switched off by annoyed lanes; receipts get kept.
   Strict mode (forge may fail builds) is a per-repo opt-in for a later version.
2. **Probe before test.** Every run starts with a shape probe so the atlas and the
   repo itself know what the repo *is* (languages, tests, qcells, ledgers).
3. **Three roots or it didn't happen.** Where seeds exist, the declared command is
   re-run under roots 7/11/23 and exit-code divergence is receipted.
4. **No tokens, no webhooks.** Telemetry is *pulled* by quilt-atlas on its existing
   6-hour schedule (see `docs/telemetry.md`). Nothing here phones home; there is
   nothing to leak and nothing to configure.
5. **Versioned like a library.** Callers pin `@v0`. We bump tags, never force-push
   them, and receipt every release of the forge itself.

## Adopt (the five-minute version)

Add one file, `.github/workflows/forge.yml`, to your repo:

```yaml
name: forge
on: [push, workflow_dispatch]
jobs:
  forge:
    uses: SuperInstance/quilt-forge/.github/workflows/forge.yml@v0
    with:
      test-cmd: node verify.mjs        # whatever a stranger would run
```

That's it. The next push probes the repo, runs your command, re-runs it under
roots 7/11/23, seals a `forge-seal.json` receipt, and the atlas will see it on its
next sweep. Python repo? Same file plus `python-version: "3.12"`.

Full options and overrides: `docs/adoption.md`.
The event schema the atlas consumes: `docs/telemetry.md`.

## What the forge is not

- Not a generic CI matrix. One job chain, one receipt shape, on purpose.
- Not a quality judge. It receipts what happened; FINDINGS.md and the qcells
  decide what it means.
- Not required. Adoption is pull, not push — repos join when a lane wants
  receipts, and absence stays UNMEASURED, never zero (atlas honesty law).

## Layout

```
.github/workflows/forge.yml   the reusable workflow
tools/forge-probe.mjs         repo shape probe (zero-dep node)
tools/forge-run.mjs           timed command runner -> receipt JSON
tools/forge-seal.mjs          consolidates probe+receipts+roots -> seal.json
templates/                    copy-paste caller workflows
docs/adoption.md              the soft-adoption contract
docs/telemetry.md             schema + how the atlas pulls it
```

## First adopters

- `qthe-verify` — PR: forge adoption (12/12 verify cases pass locally)
- `exoj` — PR: forge adoption, alongside its existing smoke.yml

Both PRs receipt the local run that preceded them. That is the whole point.
quilt-forge-main/docs/adoption.md:
# Adoption — the soft contract

Adopting the forge is adding one file. Leaving it is deleting that file. Nothing
else about your repo needs to change.

## Minimal adoption

`.github/workflows/forge.yml`:

```yaml
name: forge
on: [push, workflow_dispatch]
jobs:
  forge:
    uses: SuperInstance/quilt-forge/.github/workflows/forge.yml@v0
    with:
      test-cmd: <the command a stranger would run to check your repo works>
```

Pick the command honestly. `npm test`, `node verify.mjs`, `pytest -q`,
`python3 tools/selfplay.py --smoke` — whatever already exists. The forge receipts
whatever the command does, including failing. If your repo has no meaningful
command yet, adopt with `probe-only: true` — the shape probe alone is a useful
receipt, and it is honest to say "we only know what we are."

## Inputs

| input | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `test-cmd` | (required) | the command to run and root-replicate |
| `roots` | `"7,11,23"` | comma list; `""` disables root replication |
| `node-version` | `"22"` | node setup for tool-running |
| `python-version` | `""` | set to e.g. `"3.12"` to add setup-python |
| `probe-only` | `false` | shape probe only, no run, no roots |

## What you get per push

Artifacts on every run (whether or not your command passes):

- `forge-probe` — repo shape: file counts, languages, qcells/ledger/FINDINGS markers
- `forge-receipt` — your command's exit code and wall time
- `root-receipt-<n>` — same under FORGE_ROOT=7/11/23
- `forge-seal` — the consolidated constellation receipt + a `forge-ledger.jsonl` line

## Overrides and escape hatches

- Your command needs env? Inline it in `test-cmd` (`FOO=1 node test.mjs`) — it runs
  under `bash -lc`.
- Your command is a matrix of things? Run them sequentially in one command for now
  (`node a.mjs && node b.mjs`). A matrix mode is a v1 conversation.
- Forge itself misbehaving? `probe-only: true` keeps you on the map while you file
  an honest negative in the forge repo.
- Want redness? Not from v0. If a lane needs a hard gate, gate on the *seal
  artifact* in a second workflow you own — the forge stays soft by design.

## Versioning

Callers pin `@v0`. `v0` moves only to tagged `v0.x.y` releases; release notes are
receipted in this repo's releases. We never rewrite a published tag. When `v1`
exists, migration is a one-line change in each adopter — that is the entire cost
of the abstraction, which is the point.
